thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize the PRD for the SDK changes Acme requested. They want: client-side hedging, better backoff defaults, and a graceful streaming reconnect/resume. Can we scope this for a Q2 delivery? Need acceptance criteria + rollout plan.

sam: Ack. I think we should split into a core deliverable + stretch work. Core: reconnect/resume for streaming, safe defaults for retries/backoff, and a clear API shape. Stretch: hedging/parallel requests.

alex: +1. For API ergonomics, propose a small config surface under ClientOptions. Example: 
```js
new RedwoodClient({
  retry: { maxAttempts: 2, strategy: 'expo', baseMs: 100, maxMs: 2000 },
  stream: { reconnect: true, resumeTokenHeader: 'x-resume-token', maxReconnects: 3 }
})
```
Keep defaults conservative: retries on idempotent endpoints only, reconnect enabled for streaming.

jin: Important edge cases:
- Stream resume can cause duplicate tokens if server replays partial fragment. We need a resume token that is monotonic (offset-based) and server-side dedupe support.
- What does "exactly-once" mean for streamed tokens? We should document best-effort + client dedupe window.
- Backoff interactions with concurrency: if client-side batching pushes more concurrent requests, hedging could blow up GPU cost. Call out cost guardrails.

maria: Agreed. Draft acceptance criteria (high level):
- Functional: streaming reconnect resumes at the last acked token or provides a deterministic resume token; no more than N duplicate tokens observed in randomized test harness.
- Safety: default retry policy should not change existing non-idempotent behavior (disabled by default for generate endpoints unless user opts in).
- Performance: P95 latency delta for non-streaming endpoints < 5% when retries are enabled with default settings; tail (P99) shouldn't exceed +100ms.
- Observability: SDK emits metrics: retry_count, retry_reason, resume_attempts, duplicate_tokens_detected.
- Tests: integration matrix covering network flaps, server restarts, token-loss scenarios, and compatibility tests with Redwood runtime resume header.

sam: Nice. For scope: core PRD (2 sprints) = streaming resume + idiomatic retry config + docs + test harness. Stretch (following sprint) = hedging + auto-tuning for baseMs based on RTT.

alex: Rollout plan: feature-flagged release across SDK versions (node/python), beta customers (Acme + 2 internal apps), collect metrics for 2 weeks, then GA. Add an opt-in experiment for hedging only in beta.

jin: Acceptance test notes: create a deterministic test harness that can replay these scenarios and assert both correctness and no cost spike. Also add a stress test for hedging that verifies rate-limiting/backpressure kicks in correctly.

maria: Owner assignment & timeline:
- Product: maria (owner of PRD + customer communication)
- Eng lead: sam (implementation + perf signoff)
- Eng: alex (SDK API), jin (tests + compatibility)
Timeline: PRD + API design doc by next Tue (1819950000), RFC ready for review in 2 weeks, beta in ~6 weeks behind feature flag.

sam: One more API ergonomics callout: keep the public surface minimal. Prefer a RetryPolicy object with helpers (RetryPolicy.default(), RetryPolicy.noRetries(), RetryPolicy.custom({...})). That keeps migration tidy.

alex: And for streaming we expose a ResumeToken API: client gets tokens via onChunk callbacks, and SDK stores last-successful token. We surface resume callback so apps can persist tokens across sessions.

jin: Edge-case: mobile apps that sleep and lose connection. Resume token should have TTL or server validate resumption window. Add acceptance criterion: resume token expiry must be documented and default >= 5 minutes.

maria: Good catch. Also add docs: migration guide, example patterns for deduping in user apps, and recommended defaults for server-side resume support.

ops-bot: deploy: no active deployment triggered.

sam: Next steps: I'll spin up the PRD skeleton and API sketch tomorrow, tag you all. Please add any missing acceptance criteria as comments on the doc.

maria: Thanks — please cc @acme-eng contact once RFC is posted so they can opt into beta. :thumbsup:
